summary: This is a Git patch (code commit) from the OpenFlexure Microscope Server project, authored by Jaba Tqemaladze of the Georgia Longevity Alliance (ARGUS-OS1 contribution). It adds a `release_motors` action to the SangaboardThing class, allowing stepper motor coils to be de-energised so the microscope stage can be moved by hand and heat generation is reduced — particularly relevant for temperature-controlled enclosures such as incubators. A corresponding unit test is also included.

content_blocks.title: Commit Metadata
content_blocks.content:
Author: Jaba Tqemaladze <jaba@longevity.ge>

Repository: openflexure_microscope_server
Contribution context: Part of ARGUS-OS1 (Georgia Longevity Alliance) upstream contribution.

content_blocks.title: Commit Description / Motivation
content_blocks.content: The patch de-energises stepper motor coils via the existing 'release' command in Sangaboard firmware and pysangaboard's release_motors() method. Key motivations stated: (1) disengages holding torque so the stage can be moved by hand; (2) removes heat generated by holding motors energised — described as important in temperature-controlled enclosures (e.g. incubators). Motors are automatically re-energised by the next move. This is an instrumentation/hardware-control software change, not a biological experiment.

content_blocks.title: Code Change: sangaboard.py — release_motors method
content_blocks.content: Added a new @lt.action decorated method `release_motors(self) -> None` to the SangaboardThing class in `src/openflexure_microscope_server/things/stage/sangaboard.py`. The method acquires a hardware lock and calls `self._sangaboard.release_motors()`. Docstring notes: requires Sangaboard firmware with the 'release' command. No biological or therapeutic data is present.

content_blocks.title: Code Change: test_sangaboard.py — Unit Test
content_blocks.content: Added `test_release_motors(mock_sanga_thing)` unit test in `tests/unit_tests/test_sangaboard.py`. The test calls `mock_sanga_thing.release_motors()` and asserts that the underlying `_sangaboard.release_motors` mock was called exactly once with no arguments. This confirms the software integration but provides no experimental biological data.
